programme.title: Mindful Escapes: Breathe, Release, Restore
programme.desc: Join mindfulness expert Andy Puddicombe as he focuses on change and what we can learn from how animals adapt to changes in the world around them. Why is a chameleon's ability to alter its appearance crucial to its survival and what lessons are there from understanding how elephants grieve? Learning to be mindful can help us cope with life's stresses, and Andy shows how focusing on the sights and sounds of the natural world can help us deal with change in our lives.

programme.title: The Unseen Alistair Cooke
programme.desc: A revealing portrait of one of the most celebrated broadcasters of the 20th century, Alisdair Cooke, whose Radio 4 programme `Letter from America' spanned 58 years. Seen for the first time are extraordinary 8mm home movies shot by Cooke from 1933 onwards, charting his discovery of America, his passions and his friendships, including his close friendship with Charlie Chaplin.

programme.title: In Our Blood: The Forever Chemicals Scandal
programme.desc: In almost every respect, Bentham is a quintessential Yorkshire town: proud, close-knit and set against breathtaking countryside. Two years ago, an environmental journalist's investigation revealed it to be the most contaminated place ever recorded in the UK for PFAS - toxic so-called forever chemicals, some of which are linked to cancers and other serious illnesses. For decades, the town's main employer, Angus Fire, produced firefighting foam now believed to be the likely source of the pollution. The company routinely manufactured and tested this foam on site; the government ultimately banned it in 2025. This groundbreaking documentary reveals how those chemicals may have spread beyond the factory boundary and how a small town is coming to terms with what it means for them.
